{{short description|Ratio of sensible heat to latent heat}}
{{Refimprove|date=September 2014}}

The '''Stefan number'''<ref>{{IPAc-en|ˈ|s|t|ɛ|f|æ|n}}</ref>  ('''St''' or '''Ste''') is defined as the ratio of [[sensible heat]] to [[latent heat]]. It is given by the formula

<math>\mathrm{Ste} = \frac{c_p \Delta T}{L}, </math>

where 
* ''c<sub>p</sub>'' is the [[specific heat]],
** c<sub>p</sub> is the [[specific heat]] of solid phase in the [[freezing]] process while c<sub>p</sub> is the [[specific heat]] of liquid phase in the [[melting]] process.
* ∆''T'' is the [[temperature]] difference between phases, 
* ''L'' is the latent heat of melting.

It is a [[dimensionless]] parameter that is useful in analyzing a [[Stefan problem]]. The parameter was developed from [[Josef Stefan]]'s calculations of the rate of [[phase transition|phase change]] of [[water]] into [[ice]] on the [[polar ice caps]] and coined by G.S.H. Lock in 1969.<ref>Lock, G. S. H. (1969). On the use of asymptotic solutions to plane ice -water problems</ref> The problems origination is fully described by Vuik<ref>{{cite web |last1=Vuik |first1=C |date=1993 |title=Some historical notes about the Stefan problem |url=http://ta.twi.tudelft.nl/users/vuik/papers/DUT-TWI-93-07.pdf |publisher=Delft, University of Technology}}</ref> and further commentary on its place in [[Josef Stefan]]'s larger career can be found in <ref>Crepeau, J. (2007). Josef stefan: His life and legacy in the thermal sciences. Experimental Thermal and Fluid Science, 31(7), 795-803. doi:https://doi.org/10.1016/j.expthermflusci.2006.08.005</ref>
Same number exist for vapor to liquid phase change, [[Nombre de Jakob]].
